title: Serbian Empire
capsule: The Serbian Empire (Српско царство, Srpsko carstvo) was proclaimed in 1346 when Stefan Dušan (r. 1331–1355) crowned himself "Emperor and Autocrat of the Serbs and Romans" at Skopje, having conquered most of the Balkans from the Adriatic to the Aegean, including Albania, Macedonia, Thessaly, and Epirus. Dušan codified Byzantine-style imperial law in the Zakonik (Law Code) of 1349/1354, the most comprehensive medieval Slavic legal document. After his sudden death in 1355 the empire fragmented rapidly into regional magnate principalities; Stefan Uroš V, the last Nemanjić emperor, was unable to maintain central authority, and the empire effectively dissolved by 1371 following the catastrophic Ottoman defeat of the Serbian coalition at the Battle of Maritsa. The remaining Serbian principalities were themselves extinguished by the Ottoman conquest of Smederevo in 1459.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The empire's maximum extent under Stefan Dušan is relatively well attested through Byzantine chronicles and the Zakonik; post-1355 fragmentation boundaries are less precisely documented as authority dissolved into competing magnate domains.
